544465|2026-06.headline: Laxmi India Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~70% YoY to INR16.4 crore, NIM expanded to 11.36%, while credit cost jumped to 0.95% on vehicle loans.
544465|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong growth: AUM up 28% YoY to INR1,721.7 crore, own book up 31.7% to INR1,626.9 crore, and disbursements of INR232 crore versus INR166 crore a year ago. Profitability improved sharply, with PBT up ~72% to INR21.9 crore and PAT up ~70% to INR16.4 crore, driven by a 67 bps fall in cost of borrowing to 10.66%. Asset quality improved sequentially (GNPA 2.08%, NNPA 0.93%), but credit cost rose to INR3.69 crore (0.95%) from 0.58%, attributed mainly to vehicle finance and an extra 10% provisioning on up-money cases. Management kept FY27 PAT growth guidance of 40-45% and AUM growth of 30-35% unchanged.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR166 crore in Q1 FY26 (~+40%)

financial_highlights.value: INR3.69 crore (0.95% of avg gross loan)

financial_highlights.metric: Debt to equity / net debt to equity

segments.name: MSME (secured SME)
segments.commentary: Core vertical at ~INR1,395 crore AUM; management says core MSME and construction credit costs remain moderate. A new prime MSME product for INR25-50 lakh tickets was recently launched.

segments.name: Vehicle finance (wheels)
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR131 crore; source of the credit cost rise, attributed to older vintages in specific geographies. Acceptance criteria tightened and field follow-ups increased.

segments.name: Construction and loan against property
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR90 crore.

segments.name: Wholesale lending
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR58 crore.

segments.name: Personal loans
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR49 crore.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth target of ~30-35% annually maintained.
FY27 PAT growth guidance of ~40-45% maintained; Q1 PAT growth stated to be significantly ahead of this range, with revision to be considered after the next few quarters.
Targeted ROA of 3.5-3.75% by year-end, per analyst question and management reply.
Further 20-25 bps reduction in cost of borrowing expected over coming quarters, assuming stable global rates and no RBI hike.
Cost-to-income ratio currently below 50%; internal target ~42-44%.
Plan to add 30-35 branches across existing states in FY27; 10 added in Q1. One or two new states planned per year.
Capital raise of ~INR300-350 crore planned in roughly 1-1.5 years (start of next financial year), when leverage reaches ~3.5-4x (pre-IPO level ~4-4.5x).
capex_capacity: Branch network at 184 across six states (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra); 25 branches added over the last year, including 10 in UP and 6 in Maharashtra.
New branches reach breakeven in ~7-9 months (range 5-12 months) at an AUM of ~INR1.5-2 crore per branch; one of the 25 new branches is already at breakeven.
Branches are tiered: Tier 1 with 5-6 relationship officers, Tier 2 with 5-6, Tier 3 with 2-5.
Rajasthan (mother state, ~90 branches) remains the largest contributor; other states are expected to gain share over 3-4 years.
Digitised LOS/LMS, CKYC, RCU, eNACH and auto-dialer; only physical loan signing remains, expected to move to eSign shortly.
demand_pricing: Disbursements of INR232 crore grew ~40% YoY, ahead of 28% AUM growth; management attributes the gap to repayments and closures.
Portfolio yield broadly stable at 21.67%; NIM gain came from lower funding cost, not yield.
Management said it may pass on borrowing-cost relief to borrowers depending on asset quality and board decision.
37% of borrowers are first-time borrowers; customer base at ~43,946 vs 37,122 a year ago.
Management flagged rising competitive intensity in MSME lending and said underwriting discipline will be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How are the new branches performing versus the mature network, and what is the gestation period to steady-state productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Of 25 branches opened in the last year, one has reached breakeven. Breakeven takes about 7-9 months (5-12 months range) at branch AUM of roughly INR1.5-2 crore; Tier 1, 2 and 3 branches are staffed with 5-6, 5-6 and 2-5 relationship officers respectively.

qa_highlights.question: Over 3-5 years, what must change to move from a regional NBFC to a pan-India MSME franchise, and what is the biggest constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will enter one or two new states per year, having started in Rajasthan and expanded through Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP and Maharashtra. Management said it targets ROA of 3.5-3.75% and expects to reach it by year-end, with current ROA at 3.45%.

qa_highlights.question: What product and geographic mix changes are planned as AUM scales?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME stays the core product, with a new prime MSME product for INR25-50 lakh tickets. Plan is 30-35 branches in existing states in FY27, with 10 added in Q1. Rajasthan (about 90 branches) stays the largest state for the next 3-4 years, with other states gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise to about 1%, and is stress coming from newer geographies or vintages?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to the wheels (vehicle) portfolio, specifically older vintages in certain geographies, and said it is localised. Gopal Krishan Sain said the main P&L driver was an extra 10% provisioning on up-money transactions, with 70% of that provisioning booked so far.

qa_highlights.question: How much balance sheet capacity remains before equity is needed, given CRAR moderation from about 26% to 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to equity is 2.57x with liquidity of about INR255.9 crore. Management plans to raise about INR300-350 crore in roughly 1-1.5 years, starting next financial year, when leverage reaches about 3.5-4x (pre-IPO about 4-4.5x).

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM growth of 30-35% CAGR will be maintained. Margins depend on cost of borrowing and yield; management expects to pass some borrowing-cost relief to borrowers once cost of borrowing is in a declining phase.

qa_highlights.question: Are the El Nino and global uncertainties affecting the portfolio, and is AUM being expanded aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said global conflict has limited direct impact since customers are in Tier 2/3 cities, though crude prices raise borrower costs. It said growth is risk-based, with funding stopped or LTV reduced where stress is seen, and collection efficiency is expected to be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What were the net slippages in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Net slippages were INR3.26 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much further can cost of borrowing fall, what is the sustainable NIM, and where can cost-to-income settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Piyush Somani said another 20-25 bps reduction is expected over coming quarters, assuming stable global rates and no RBI hike; incremental cost of borrowing is about 10.48% over the last 12 months. Cost-to-income is below 50% now, with an internal target of around 42-44%; opex is elevated by new-state branch openings.

qa_highlights.question: How should the gap between 40% disbursement growth and 28% AUM growth be read, and does the run rate support faster AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Kuldeep Singh said the gap reflects repayments and loan closures, and that the current disbursement run rate supports AUM growth.

risks_watch: Vehicle (wheels) finance credit cost: rose to 0.95% of average gross loan (INR3.69 crore) from 0.58%; watch whether the older-vintage stress in specific geographies eases after tighter acceptance criteria and more field follow-ups.
Up-money cases: an extra 10% provisioning is being applied, with 70% of ECL provision booked so far; further provisioning depends on court-led enforcement and collection progress.
Capital: CRAR moderated to 25.32% from about 26%, and a INR300-350 crore raise is planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; execution timing and dilution are open.
Margin sustainability: NIM gain came from funding cost (10.66%, down 67 bps), not yield; management expects only 20-25 bps further cost reduction and may pass some relief to borrowers.
Branch maturity: new branches take 7-9 months on average to breakeven (range 5-12 months); cost-to-income is still above the 42-44% target, and opex grew about 34% YoY.

Competitive intensity in MSME lending is rising; management said underwriting discipline will be maintained. ROA target of 3.5-3.75% and FY27 PAT guidance of 40-45% (Q1 already well ahead) are to be reviewed after the next few quarters.
key_quotes: At the same time, we remain conscious that as we scale, maintaining the quality of our portfolio and discipline our underwriting will remain the most important priority for us.
We believe this is prudent to maintain our existing guidance at this stage and assess the performance over the next few quarters before considering any revision.
We are not looking to grow simply for the sake of balance sheet expansion.
The only manual step remains in our process is physical signing of loan agreements which we expect to move to eSign shortly.

544466|2026-03.headline: Aditya Infotech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore with EBITDA margin of 18%; FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore.
544466|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore, with EBITDA up 162% to INR258.3 crore and margin up 800 bps to 18%, helped by price rise, low-cost inventory and SKU mix. Full-year FY26 revenue reached INR4,220.8 crore (+35.6%), EBITDA INR579 crore (13.7% margin) and adjusted PAT INR368 crore (+166.1%). Management raised FY27 guidance to revenue INR6,000-6,500 crore, EBITDA margin 14-15% and PAT margin 8.5-9.5%. Management flagged that low-cost inventory is now exhausted and component costs (chips, memory, USD, freight) will keep rising through 2027, so price increases are being passed on monthly in small steps.

financial_highlights.change: Debt repaid from IPO proceeds; Q4 finance cost down 38%

segments.name: CP PLUS brand
segments.commentary: Contributed 86% of AIL revenue in Q4 and FY26; IP products are 73% of the CP PLUS portfolio.

segments.name: Camera/CCTV (India market)
segments.commentary: Company market share about 45.4% as of Q3 FY26, versus about 30% overall and about 25% for CP PLUS at the start of the journey. Management says it is not targeting a specific share number.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore, about 50% growth over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 14-15%; PAT margin around 8.5-9.5%. Management called 14-15% the new normal for FY27 and FY28, with Q4 a one-off above that level.
Unit volume growth target 25-30%, against an industry CCTV unit growth estimate of 15-16%.
Average per-unit camera realisation expected to rise 20-25% in FY27 (analyst-cited ASP growth about 25%).
FY27 capex expected at INR200-300 crore, funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.
FY28 vision: double production capacity versus current levels, complete backward integration in key components, and a fully functional global R&D presence including Taiwan.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity has reached 2.5 million units; management targets 90-100% utilisation.
Housing plant: Phase-1 operational by Q2 FY27 and Phase-2 by Q4 FY27, targeting 30 million housings and enclosures per year.
New lens assembly line commissioning with initial capacity of 5 lakh lenses per month, scalable to 1 million per month; CCTV lens production to start soon at Kadapa.
Kadapa: acquiring additional land and adding a 50,000 sq ft shed. Noida: proposed 3 lakh sq ft facility in Sector 68, operational by Q4 FY27.
Orient Cables JV for LAN and CCTV cable manufacturing: plant in Rajasthan (about 1 lakh sq ft), commercial operations expected between Q2 and Q3 FY27.
HD analog job work planned to move to EMS partners at about 0.5 million units per month. Evaluating further land in North India.
demand_pricing: Price hike of 6-8% taken in January 2026; management now moves prices monthly in small steps (single-digit % per month, varying by category) to avoid shocking customers. Further increases expected in FY27.

Market unit growth expected at 15-16% for FY27. Management says the industry's pent-up demand from the STQC transition was muted in FY26, and ASP increases are heavier on entry-level IP and NVR than on enterprise/project segments.
Consumer purchases are under 10% of the business; the business is largely B2B. Government is 15-20% of revenue and management plans for a similar share.

Competition: about 30 certified brands. A dozen global brands hold about 10% share; about 1.5 dozen domestic brands are each far smaller (about one-tenth of AIL's size or less). Management sees no single clear number-two player.
Memory: half of the 6-7 non-China DDR makers have stopped DDR3 output, pushing supply tightness onto smaller players. Management says scale lets AIL secure supply ahead of competitors.
Volume vs value in FY26: volume growth about 18-20%, with the rest from ASP and mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 gross margin (about 31.8%) came from low-cost inventory, mix or price rise, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair cited a mix of low-cost inventory, the Q4 price rise and higher-end SKUs (STQC-certified project SKUs from H2). He said the low-cost inventory is now mostly used up, but FY27 guidance is above FY26 and slightly below Q4 margin.

qa_highlights.question: Cash conversion cycle and working capital needs with advance chip and memory purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said the cash conversion cycle has risen because creditors fell as the company secured supply, and some inventory is being blocked with advance payments. Working capital is factored into FY27 plans; capex is to be funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said the earlier plan of about INR200 crore has been raised to INR200-300 crore for FY27, with FY28 plans still under work. Funding is through internal accruals and some debt; the debt-equity ratio is very low.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14-15% EBITDA margin the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said 14-15% should be the new normal for FY27 and FY28, driven by localisation, cost optimisation, the shift to higher-end and enterprise products and premiumisation. Q4 was a one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Export plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said export action may start in FY27, but domestic demand comes first. Some thoughts are underway and the outcome is not yet clear.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split FY26: volume vs price?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said volume growth was about 18-20% and the rest came from ASP and mix. The price rise was mainly in Q4. For FY27, ASP growth is about 25% and volume growth 25-30%.

risks_watch: Chip and memory supply: lead times are long, contracts are being invalidated under force majeure, and management says costs are rising every fortnight to week. Watch whether monthly price increases keep pace.
Margin sustainability: low-cost inventory is used up, and the cash conversion cycle has lengthened due to advance payments and lower creditors.
Demand: entry-level IP and NVR demand may shift to analog as price rises. Consumer and mobile-style demand softness is a risk in the wider market.
Execution: housing plant (Phase-1 Q2 FY27), lens line, Noida facility (Q4 FY27) and Rajasthan cable JV (Q2-Q3 FY27) all need to meet timelines. Doubling capacity by FY28 is a target.

New brands: Nexivue has started shipping since April 2026. Eyra is delayed by R&D rework and may reach market next quarter. Qualcomm AI platform is in trials and commercial rollout is phased. Certification pace is a watch item.
Competition: a more certified competitor base could arrive from 2028 onward, according to the analyst's question. Management says it has a head start on localisation, capacity and supply.

544466|2026-06.headline: Aditya Infotech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 89.5% YoY to INR1,402 crore; EBITDA margin 14.8%, adjusted PAT INR142.2 crore.

EBITDA rose 20% YoY to INR208 crore, with margin up 604 bps to 14.8%, helped by product and brand mix and operating efficiencies. Gross margin was 30.8%, up 8-10 bps YoY but moderated from Q4 as lower-cost inventory was exhausted. Adjusted PAT of INR142.2 crore rose 332.5% YoY, aided by a 59% fall in finance costs; management reiterated its FY27 EBITDA guidance of 14-15%.

segments.name: CP PLUS (brand)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 87% of Q1 revenue; IP products were about 79% of the CP PLUS portfolio, reflecting shift to higher-value AI surveillance.

segments.name: Nexivue (second brand)
segments.commentary: Rollout being accelerated in coming months with a wider portfolio to extend channel coverage; no revenue disclosed.

FY27 revenue guidance cited by an analyst as INR60-65 billion; management did not dispute it on the call.
Price increases of 10-20% taken so far by product; expected 15-20% cumulative by end of H1 and about 25% for FY27 overall.
Backward-integration plants (housing and enclosures) operational by Q3 FY27; in-house scale manufacturing to kick off in Q3-Q4 FY27.
CP PLUS Pro series and Home IoT products targeted to go live by end-Q3/beginning-Q4 FY27; exports expected to be significant in 18-24 months.
Corelink Cable JV (with Orient Cables) to start commercial production by end of FY27.

Corelink Cable JV plant in Rajasthan of about 1 lakh sq ft, expected commercial production by end of FY27.

Management attributed the H2 shortfall to component price inflation and lengthened lead times, and said it chose to defer unviable fixed-price contracts and protect the balance sheet. Total liabilities fell from Rs 50 crore to Rs 12.20 crore and trade payables from Rs 30.21 crore to Rs 3.77 crore.

544482|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 6% to INR88.5 crore and EBITDA 17% to INR33.2 crore (37.5% margin), with management guiding 25-30% growth for FY27.
544482|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations grew about 6% to INR88.5 crore, while EBITDA rose 17% to INR33.2 crore and margin expanded 330 bps to 37.5%. PAT grew 21% to INR19.3 crore, and operating cash flow turned positive at INR23.4 crore versus negative INR2.6 crore (call transcript cites INR22.6 crore) in FY25. Management attributed the weak top-line to regulatory delays (PNDT, AERB) on new centre openings and said these are now resolved, backing 25-30% growth in FY27. The company reported net cash of about INR31 crore and total debt of INR20.6 crore at March 2026.

544484|2026-03.headline: BlueStone Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 49.1% YoY; SSG of 34% and FY26 revenue of INR 2,441 crore, with 340 stores after 65 added in FY26.
544484|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone revenue up 49.1% YoY and FY26 revenue of INR 2,441 crore, with same-store sales growth of 34% spread evenly across all three months. The store base reached 340 stores in 134 cities after adding 17 stores in Q4 and 65 in FY26, below the 83 added in FY25 and below the RHP plan of 290 stores over FY26-FY27. Management said pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins improved YoY despite a mix shift toward plain gold, and attributed the recovery to rapid entry-level repricing and vertical integration. Gold price inflation inflated closing inventory, which pushed inventory turns down to about 1.13x from 1.3x in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: Franchisee store count and plan for them?
qa_highlights.answer: About 67 of 340 stores are franchisee-owned; the model was used as a capital structure tool, and FY27-FY28 should see a substantial drop as contracts (5 years) run down.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory turns fall from about 1.3x to 1.13x despite fewer store adds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the fall mainly to a one-off rise in closing inventory value from gold prices. Mature stores (3-4+ years) run at 1.7x-1.9x turns.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the store plan been cut from 290 in the RHP to 65 in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slowdown was a tactical call tied to gold-price demand conviction, and Q4 added 17 stores, a pickup. It reaffirmed about 20% annual distribution growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 34% SSSG sustainable as stores mature?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY20 SSSG was near 30%, Q2-Q3 FY25 was the anomaly from the gold spike, and Q4 is a return to normal. Growth is spread across old and new cohorts.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall QoQ and YoY on mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said YoY is the right comparison because costs are largely fixed; pre-Ind AS margin improved YoY despite the mix shift.

qa_highlights.question: How will gross margin hold if plain gold keeps rising in mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said plain gold is additive, not substitutive, premium pricing holds, and operating leverage will expand EBITDA and capital productivity; it declined to give a numeric offset.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ESOP cost up about 80%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ESOPs are a management-only plan (about 90% held by the top six), 50-60% granted pre-IPO, with front-loaded accounting charges of INR 93 crore, then 58, then 28 crore; unallocated pool is about 1.7%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no forward-looking revenue guidance.

544484|2026-06.headline: BlueStone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR 733 crore, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 135% to INR 55 crore and margin at 7.5%.
544484|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 49% YoY to INR 733 crore and pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 135% to INR 55 crore, lifting operating margin to 7.5% (up 273 bps). Management attributed this to operating leverage despite a custom duty hike on gold from 6% to 15% that softened demand in May before June and July recovered. Same-store sales growth was 39%, repeat revenue share rose to about 60%, while new customer additions reportedly fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management tied to merchandise dislocation during the sharp gold rise. Management reiterated a long-term target of roughly INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years, around 30% SSSG and about 20% store distribution growth, though analysts questioned the arithmetic.

financial_highlights.value: About INR 50 crore, about 6.9% of revenue
financial_highlights.change: Flat vs 6.9% in same quarter last year

segments.commentary: Management said more than 80% of sales originate online, with stores converting intent built online. Company describes itself as a consumer internet business that sells jewellery.

segments.commentary: Network of 352 stores; recent stores are around 4,500 sq ft frontage, and management said operational sq ft and per-store unit economics are unchanged. Store additions guided to about 20% CAGR over four years, with a 70-80 annual run rate referenced.

segments.commentary: About 95% of products sold are manufactured in-house; management estimates a 300-400 bps margin delta versus peers but stresses design control as the main rationale.

Operating EBITDA margin expected to expand from 7.5% toward about 15% over four years, driven mainly by corporate and marketing scale leverage.

Around 20% distribution (store) CAGR guided over next four years; store additions expected to be non-linear.
demand_pricing: Demand softened in May after the gold import duty hike (6% to 15%), then recovered through June; management said July trends were similar to June.
Gold exchange volumes rose as gold prices climbed; management said no significant change in the last 1-2 weeks.
New customer additions fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management attributed to merchandise dislocation; repeat revenue growth was strong.
Repeat AOVs are said to be 20-30% higher than new-customer AOVs; blended AOV about INR 78,000.
Management says no 9-carat plans; 14-carat experiments are used in lower price points. Lab-grown diamonds are said to be under 1% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand trending into July after the May softness from the duty hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand softened in May, recovered through June, and July is tracking similarly to June with no major difference.

qa_highlights.question: How should growth be thought of in H2 as gold inflation tapers, and the company lapping sharp gold rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stable gold is most supportive for demand and that Q3 last year was its slowest quarter in history during the sharpest gold rise; it does not expect a headwind.

qa_highlights.question: Why has new customer addition fallen to about 40,000 and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the drop, attributed it to merchandise dislocation being fixed, and said month-on-month new customer trends are improving.

qa_highlights.question: Math behind the 50% revenue CAGR given 30% SSSG and 20% distribution growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% refers to mature-cohort SSSG at maturity (years 3-6), not reported SSSG, and that reported SSSG would be higher due to new stores.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin expanded about 100 bps excluding inventory gain; what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix changes in studded share were not material; contribution margin, the more relevant metric, has been largely stable, and EBITDA expansion comes from operating leverage.

qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about INR 2,800 crore at end June versus INR 2,650 crore in March; management said store additions and gold prices drive the balance and turns should improve.

qa_highlights.question: Why 20% distribution growth rather than a slower pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most operating leverage comes from corporate and marketing scale rather than store-level profit, so faster distribution growth is preferred.

qa_highlights.answer: Marketing was about INR 50 crore, 6.9% of revenue, same as last year; it fell from about 9.2% four years ago to 6.6% in FY26.

544487|2026-06.headline: Patel Retail Q1 FY27 total income rose 69.35% YoY to INR310.24 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to about 6.3% on raw material intensity.
544487|2026-06.overview: Total income reached INR310.24 crores, up 69.35% YoY from INR183.19 crores, while EBITDA grew 23.92% to INR19.68 crores and PAT rose 37.43% to INR9.52 crores (EPS INR2.85). Management attributed the margin compression (about 133 bps decline cited, and a 233 bps figure also mentioned) to a higher raw-material-intensity mix in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked business amid volatile raw material prices and odd order timing. The company added stores at Rasayani and Babgaon in Q1 and opened its 53rd store at Uran (Raigad) after quarter-end, and expanded Indian Chaska into Madhya Pradesh. Management guided to positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 and 8 to 10 new stores in FY27.

544495|2026-06.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Systems revenue to rise from INR13-14 crore to about INR30 crore this year via CCTV and command-centre subscription models (HDFC 100-150 branches, INR2-3 crore revenue), though no named product launch was given.

rows.why: Q1 order wins of INR45.71 crore (Reliance and Nesco) are booked, but the INR15-18 crore Mumbai traffic and INR6 crore NKDA AMC tenders are not yet awarded and drive the CCTV ~INR30 crore target.

rows.label: FCF lift to INR13-14 crore
rows.why: Average FCF was INR8-9 crore over 3-4 years; target is to lift it to INR13-14 crore by growing systems revenue to about INR30 crore, but management also says debt stays flat.

tone.note: Management was confident on order inflows, the INR500 crore FY27 and INR630-650 crore FY28 revenue targets, but cautious and evasive on margin expansion, buyback and the share price fall, deflecting to growth capex; analysts pressed on net debt, buyback and margin path.

544496|2026-03.headline: Vikran FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,249 crore (vs INR916 crore) with EBITDA margin near 14%; FY27 guided at INR2,200 crore plus.
544496|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR647 crore, up from INR355 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR92 crore (14.2% margin) and PAT of INR56 crore (vs INR38 crore). For FY26, revenue rose to INR1,249 crore, EBITDA was about INR175 crore (around 14%) and PAT was INR92 crore (vs about INR78 crore). Management attributed margin dilution to delayed Jal Jeevan Mission receivables (provisioned, mostly in Q4), and to early-stage solar EPC projects. The company closed its acquisition of NOPL Solar (969 MW PM-KUSUM project) at end-April 2026 and guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200 crore plus, with a 14-15% EBITDA margin target.

vs INR916 crore in FY25; highest in company history

financial_highlights.value: upgraded to IND A, stable outlook

segments.name: Power T&D
segments.commentary: Management sees FY27 power T&D at about 30% of revenue, focused on selective 765 kV GIS/AIS projects for clients such as Power Grid and NTPC. Scope includes substations, lines, underground cabling and smart metering.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Solar is now the main growth pillar, with management expecting about 60% of FY27 revenue. Marquee wins include 100 MW AC (Ellume Energy), 400 MW AC / 580 MWp DC (NTPC Renewable) and 600 MW (NOPL Solar); 20 MW of NOPL is commissioned, with more due by end-May.

segments.name: Water infrastructure
segments.commentary: Water is about 10% of FY27 revenue from the existing order book, roughly INR600 crore; no new water bids for about 18 months. Jal Jeevan Mission receivables are about INR400 crore, and INR17-18 crore was received in FY27 to date.

segments.name: NOPL Solar (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Acquired 100% at end-April 2026; project cost INR4,200 crore with sanctioned lender funding. Management cites revenue over INR500 crore over 25 years, 85-88% EBITDA margin, and about INR1 crore per month from the first 20 MW.

EBITDA margin guided at 14-15% for FY27, which management said it was confident of maintaining.
Possible additional INR1,000-1,400 crore solar EPC order from the Onix balance EPC scope, not yet in the INR5,700 crore order book; may be booked at arm's length price.

Data centre EPC target of about INR100 crore order book in FY27, initially 50-100 MW.

Management is cautiously evaluating Middle East and Africa opportunities, and says it is not pursuing a developer or investment model for data centres.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin recover from 13-14% to historical 18-22%, and what is the status of the Onix project and its financing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY23-25 EBITDA was 15-17%, with FY26 at about 14% due to JJM receivable provisions (reversed on collection). Management said the Onix SPV is now 100% owned; the lender is comfortable, and 4 projects are commissioned with 2 more due by end-May.

qa_highlights.question: What is execution in FY27 with and without NOPL, and what milestones have been achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says INR2,200 crore plus is achievable with or without NOPL, and that a plan without NOPL 'does not make a lot of sense'. Milestones since the April takeover are limited to a few commissioned projects; land and evacuation issues are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: How much receivables exposure is there from water/JJM, and how much was provided in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR400 crore of water receivables are due from JJM. About INR20 crore of provision was taken in FY26, mostly in Q4; the CFO said there is no specific high-risk receivable.

qa_highlights.question: When will cash flow turn positive, and will there be equity dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there are no plans for further equity dilution and that operating cash flow is expected to turn positive from FY28; the order book has grown from about INR2,000 crore to over INR5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said about 60% solar, 30% power T&D and about 10% water.

qa_highlights.question: Is the additional INR1,400 crore NOPL solar order included in the INR5,700 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not included because the order is not yet placed and documentation is pending; the CFO said about INR1,000 crore may be booked in coming days, executable over 12-15 months.

risks_watch: Working capital: payables up about 60% to INR788 crore and receivables about INR1,000 crore; operating cash flow remains negative.

NOPL execution: about 85% land identified, 150-odd locations to complete by March 2027 deadline; the lender line roll-over is subject to a promoter evaluation.
Pending INR1,000-1,400 crore Onix balance EPC order (arm's length pricing) that would be additional to the INR5,700 crore order book.
Supply-chain and geopolitical risk from China sourcing and the West Asia conflict; management is hedging with large suppliers.
Data centre EPC entry, with a small INR100 crore target; no formal order yet.

Several figures were corrected mid-call (NOPL monthly revenue, water receivables).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR2,200 crore plus versus INR1,249 crore in FY26 (about 76% growth), with the order book at INR5,700 crore and solar expected at about 60% of FY27 revenue.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure was given, and the company is asset-light EPC with a large NOPL project already funded (INR4,200 crore sanctioned), so a new capex announcement is not signalled; only the data centre EPC entry (INR100 crore target) is a small possibility.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of INR2,200 crore plus is backed by a INR5,700 crore order book (up from about INR2,000 crore), and a possible INR1,000-1,400 crore Onix balance EPC order is not yet in the book, but conversion timing is not quantified.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Operating cash flow is still negative with receivables about INR1,000 crore (vs INR605 crore), payables up to INR788 crore, about INR400 crore of JJM receivables, and NOPL execution must reach 148 MW advanced stage with about 150 locations to complete by March 2027.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launch was discussed; the nearest item is a data centre EPC entry targeting about INR100 crore of orders in FY27, which is an entry into a service line, not a product launch.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turns positive from FY28
rows.why: Management said operating cash flow is expected to turn positive from FY28, but it remains negative today with receivables about INR1,000 crore against payables of INR788 crore.

rows.label: Onix balance EPC order of INR1,000-1,400 crore
rows.why: CFO said about INR1,000 crore may be booked in coming days, executable over 12-15 months, but documentation is pending and the order is not yet placed or in the INR5,700 crore book.

rows.label: No further equity dilution
rows.why: Management said no further equity dilution is planned while NOPL funding of INR4,200 crore is sanctioned and backup financing is in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 revenue of INR2,200 crore plus and the 14-15% margin, but cautious on receivables, cash flow and the Onix/NOPL details; analysts pushed on the margin recovery, the INR5,700 crore order-book figure, and whether the Onix order is included.

544496|2026-06.headline: Vikran Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 28.2% YoY to INR204 crore and PAT 209.9% to INR17.5 crore, while consolidated PAT was only INR4 crore.

segments.commentary: About 10% of order book; about INR12 crores of Q1 revenue. Carries a provision of about INR6.5 crores due to slow Jal Jeevan Mission receivables recovery; about INR120 crores of debtors are tied to JJM projects.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue from NOPL in standalone INR204 crores and why growth only 28%?
qa_highlights.answer: NOPL contributed about INR62 crores; management attributed low H1 to seasonality and client budget constraints, with H2 expected to be heavy against INR2,200-2,500 crores FY27 execution target.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins dip in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited higher project costs, about INR6.5 crores provision on Jal Jeevan receivables (reversible on collection), and NOPL overheads booked without revenue at consolidated level; standalone margins described as normal.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated revenue lower than standalone and which to track?

qa_highlights.question: Status of Jal Jeevan Mission receivables and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital in JJM projects fixed at a set level; about INR120 crores of JJM debtors; about INR23 crores received last quarter and more than INR10 crores in the last 30 days, with central funds of about INR17,000 crores released to UP.

qa_highlights.question: Status of NOPL debt financing (INR3,100 crores) from IREDA and other lenders?

qa_highlights.question: Debtor days at 296 — has it peaked?

544497|2026-03.headline: Anlon FY26 consolidated income rose 42.98% to INR 172.22 crore and PAT 41.77% to INR 29.09 crore, but Q4 PAT fell to INR 11.07 crore from INR 16.65 crore.
544497|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated total income of INR 172.22 crore (+42.98% YoY), EBITDA of INR 47.77 crore (+47.55%) and PAT of INR 29.09 crore (+41.77%), driven by the Apiqo and Bizotic acquisitions. Q4 total income rose to INR 50.90 crore from INR 48.97 crore, but PBT was flat at INR 14.44 crore and PAT fell to INR 11.07 crore, which management attributed to higher operating and development expenses and raw material cost spikes linked to the Middle East conflict. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR 380-400 crore, FY28 to INR 700-800 crore in one answer (INR 600-700 crore in another), and consolidated EBITDA margin of 24-25% as a floor, with a sharp reduction in receivables and cash-flow positivity targeted by end FY27. Several answers were inconsistent (EBITDA margin guidance ranged from 24-25% to 30-35%; FY28 revenue from 600-700 to 700-800 crore), and the call was disrupted by poor audio for several analysts.

vs INR 15.49 crore in Q4 FY25
vs INR 16.65 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: 130-140 days on average (some domestic customers 150 days)
-INR 23 crore prior period to -INR 47 crore after consolidation

segments.name: Pharmaceutical intermediates and APIs (Anlon standalone)
segments.commentary: Management says 5-6 DMF-linked products are already supplied to regulated markets, with 5-7 more expected to commercialise in FY27; export share targeted at about 60% in FY27. Products cited include Ketoprofen, Dexketoprofen and Loxoprofen Sodium in the NSAID category.

segments.name: Apiqo Organics (acquired, early Jan 2026 per management)
segments.commentary: Acquired and consolidated for about 2.5 months in FY26. Management said its EBITDA margin is structurally lower (approx. 22-23%) as a chemical/intermediate manufacturer, and backward integration into intermediates is planned to start from Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Bizotic Life Science (acquired)
segments.commentary: Consolidated for about 15 days in FY26. Management expects margins close to Anlon's, and says backward integration of intermediates has run for three to four years.

segments.name: Industrial and fine/specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Early-traction vertical; management is discussing a dedicated Apiqo capacity expansion with one or two customers, with margins slightly below pharma. No revenue figure was disclosed.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Three molecules in development for two global innovators. One is in validation with batches of hundreds of kg since March; commercial supply expected by Q3 FY27, with the other two in validation by Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 380-400 crore, with a clear order book of INR 280-300 crore and a further INR 80-90 crore expected from products under qualification.
FY28 revenue guided at INR 700-800 crore in one answer and INR 600-700 crore in another, assuming 50-60% utilisation of the new Rajkot capacity from Q1 FY28 (six months of trial and validation).

Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 24-25% as a floor, with management saying it will not sell below levels that breach that margin; a separate answer cited 30-35% for FY27 and the closing remarks used 25-30%.
Consolidated PAT: conservative FY27 estimate of INR 45 crore; management agreed INR 50-55 crore is achievable when asked.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive on an annual basis by end FY27; management said it was '100% sure'.
Revenue CAGR of approx. 30% over three years stated in prepared remarks; peak revenue potential of the current 1,400-1,600 MTPA capacity stated at INR 450-500 crore at 80% utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined installed capacity after Apiqo and Bizotic: approx. 1,400-1,600 MTPA; consolidated utilisation approx. 62-65%, with management saying practical maximum is about 85%.

New greenfield capex at the existing Rajkot premises estimated at INR 130 crore; plant layout under approval, construction to start end of the month or early next month, commercial production targeted by Q1 FY28 (also referred to as mid-FY28).

Funding: term loan of INR 65-70 crore (about 50-60% of capex), balance from internal accruals; equipment orders placed 6-8 months ahead, with advance payments already made and part of the equipment installed.
Standalone peak revenue with expansion stated at INR 400-450 crore.
Capex and expansion of QC capacity already under way; management is considering a further INR 130 crore-type expansion to scale specialty chemicals at Apiqo, subject to customer commitments.
demand_pricing: Management said raw material prices (solvents, catalysts) have more than doubled since the conflict, and prices change daily; Q4 margin pressure came from holding purchase orders at old prices, and customers are now being asked to pay higher prices as a force majeure.
Management said price increases are being negotiated and expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin to be close to the prior full-year level, but acknowledged this is uncertain if geopolitical conditions worsen.

Ketoprofen US DMF is delayed: a customer will file on Anlon's behalf, and timing has moved from Q2 FY27 to Q3 or Q4 FY27. Dexketoprofen Europe DMF is at the EDQM query stage, expected to close in two to three months.

Competitive positioning: few Indian players in Ketoprofen and Dexketoprofen (two to three in India, five to six globally); management cites proprietary methylation and Friedel-Crafts chemistry and landing-cost advantage.

Receivables: a distributor dispute left INR 20-30 crore pending in late 2025; INR 11 crore recovered and about INR 17 crore still outstanding. Management has stopped supply to customers paying beyond 120 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue outlook and the peak potential of the current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 visibility is INR 380-400 crore; peak revenue from 1,400-1,600 MTPA is INR 450-500 crore at about 80% utilisation (management said the practical ceiling is 85%).

qa_highlights.question: How much order book is in place and what are the CDMO timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Clear order book is INR 280-300 crore, with INR 80-90 crore more expected. One CDMO product is in validation, with commercial supply expected by Q3 FY27; the other two validations by Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook, and why did Q4 fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided consolidated margin of 24-25% as a floor; Q4 fell because of unrecovered raw material cost increases, higher operating costs and the acquisitions. Management expects Q1 FY27 margins to recover to roughly the prior full-year level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the funding plan for the capex, working capital and any acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is funded with INR 65-70 crore of term loans and internal accruals; management said there is no current equity dilution plan, with rights issue or promoter unsecured loans as possible options later. Working capital may need cash credit from banks after commissioning.

qa_highlights.question: What is the receivables outlook and cash-flow timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days are 130-140 on average, and management expects them to stay at or above 180 days (per one answer), while also saying payments are running at 100-105 days now. Cash flow expected positive on an annual basis in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Credit rating and minority buy-out status?

Management plans to acquire the remaining minority stake in Apiqo and Bizotic through share swaps, likely at the next AGM.

Ketoprofen US DMF timing slipped to Q3 or Q4 FY27 through a customer filing; Dexketoprofen Europe DMF at EDQM query stage, expected to close in two to three months.
FY28 revenue guidance differs between INR 600-700 crore and INR 700-800 crore; FY27 PAT conservative INR 45 crore versus INR 50-55 crore said achievable.

544497|2026-06.headline: Anlon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~17% (PAT ₹8.28 cr) on raw-material spikes and Remember India consolidation; management targets 25-27% for FY27.
544497|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 total income was ₹87.62 cr versus ₹33.31 cr in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of ₹15.65 cr (vs ₹6.26 cr) and PAT of ₹8.28 cr (vs ₹3.55 cr). EBITDA margin moderated to about 17%, which management attributed to a sharp rise in solvent and petrochemical raw-material prices after the geopolitical conflict and to operating costs of the newly acquired Remember India Health links being consolidated. The company completed the 63.98% acquisition of Remember India on 8 May 2026, has acquired Apiqo Organics and Bizotic Lifesciences, and is moving into finished dosage formulations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr and a ~30% three-year revenue CAGR, but gave limited quantitative detail on Remember India.

financial_highlights.change: moderated; management earlier guided ~24-25% floor for Q1

segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹30-32 cr, down from ₹33 cr YoY per analyst; management says it is at peak utilisation and expects FY27 standalone revenue of ~₹180 cr. Production cycles of 30-45 days mean some output lands in Q2.

segments.name: Apiqo Organics (68% stake, moving to 100%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹45 cr, described as the most profitable unit; FY27 revenue expected ₹120-150 cr. Business is fully booked in industrial and fine chemicals; share-swap to make it a 100% subsidiary to complete by end-Q2.

segments.name: Bizotic Lifesciences (57% stake, moving to 100%)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue ~₹12 cr; FY27 expected ~₹60 cr. Management says it is profitable and that committed partner business exists; share-swap to 100% also targeted by end-Q2.

segments.name: Remember India Health links (63.98%)
segments.commentary: Finished dosage formulations (tablets, capsules, ointments) with access to 30+ dossiers; in investment and turnaround phase. No revenue assumed for FY27 until at least Q4 FY27; WHO-PQ approval expected by end-CY2026. Margin expected above 25%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr reiterated; management said H1 comparison is the right lens, and the guidance range was re-confirmed as ₹380-400 cr in one answer.
EBITDA margin: ~17% in Q1; management expects margins to improve from Q2 (said 'better than the first quarter') and target 25-27% for FY27 on consolidated basis; earlier comment of 22-25% in H1.
Gross margin expected to hold at 40-45%.
FY28 revenue indicated at ~₹700 cr if Anlon-site expansion (~₹130 cr capex, ~1,200 MT additional) is commissioned on schedule by Q1 FY28; management flagged possible delays from statutory approvals.

Working capital: receivable days expected to fall toward 60-70 days over time (current ~130-135 days vs 90-day terms); management expects positive operating cash flow in FY27, 'lower but positive'. Management also said H1 operating cash flow positive is targeted before year-end.
Biologics subsidiary (Anlon Biologics) revenue expected from Q4 FY28; Anlon Medicare from Q2 FY28; Remember India peak revenue/EBITDA to be detailed in Q2 call.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity after three acquisitions stated at ~1,400-1,600 MT per annum; management clarified Anlon standalone is ~400 MT and is at peak.
Anlon-site expansion: ~₹130 cr capex adding ~1,200 MT (standalone to ~1,600 MT); commissioning targeted by Q1 FY28 subject to statutory approvals.
Funding: ~₹70 cr debt at ~8.5-8.6% interest; balance from internal accruals.
Eight new cleanrooms planned at the new facility to run eight APIs in parallel; initial planning assumes 50-60% utilisation.
Bizotic and Apiqo utilisation can rise gradually from ~65% toward higher levels; no 65-to-85% jump expected within this year.
Anlon Biologics (peptides, biosimilars) construction to begin within ~2 months; in-house peptide manufacturing targeted by FY28.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices: management said solvent/methanol-linked inputs rose 2-3x since pre-war (methanol cited at ₹22 to ₹58-60/kg); not yet normalised. Around 40% of API manufacturing cost is solvents and petroleum-linked inputs.

Price pass-through: price increases on finished products have been initiated and customers have agreed; management expects this to reflect over the next one to two quarters, but earlier orders at old prices weighed on Q1.
Customer base is concentrated: 10-15 B2B customers, which limits ability to reprice frequently.
Fine/specialty chemicals (Apiqo): fully booked, described as 'overbooked'; management estimates ₹120-150 cr contribution in FY27.
CDMO: expected commercial supply of first molecule by Q3 and others by Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28; process validations ongoing.
Seven new APIs/DMFs planned for filing within FY27; compilation under way.

qa_highlights.question: Have raw material prices normalised, and by which quarter will EBITDA margins recover? Will Q2 margins be similar to Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: RM prices not normalised; solvent/methanol-linked inputs up 2-3x (methanol ~₹22 to ₹58-60/kg). Management expects margin normalisation by Q3 and said Q2 would be better than Q1, with price increases reflecting over one to two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 revenue outlook versus ~₹87 cr Q1 run-rate and capacity utilisation (~62%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated ₹350-400 cr as peak-level potential and said utilisation is ~65-70%; asked to compare H1 rather than quarter-on-quarter because production cycles run 15-40+ days.

qa_highlights.question: Segment revenue contribution in Q1 and expected FY27 split?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1: Apiqo ~₹45 cr, Anlon standalone ~₹32 cr, Bizotic ~₹11.5-12 cr. FY27 expectations: Apiqo ₹120-150 cr, Anlon standalone ~₹180 cr, Bizotic ~₹60 cr; Remember India not included until Q3/Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why has EBITDA margin declined over the last two quarters, and what is the FY27 consolidated margin expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to temporary geopolitical RM spike with customers on prior-price orders, plus lower-margin acquired units and Remember India costs. Management guided 25-27% consolidated EBITDA for FY27 and said Q2 would sustain around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Remember India revenue and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY27 revenue assumed; WHO-PQ approval expected by end-CY2026; detailed projection deferred to Q2 call. Management said margins should be above 25% due to in-house API backward integration.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital, receivable days and operating cash flow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables run ~130-135 days versus 90-day terms; management expects reduction toward 60-70 days over time and 'lower but positive' operating cash flow in FY27, targeted before year-end. Inventory is development stock held 9-12 months pending DMF approval.

qa_highlights.question: Interest rate on the ~₹70 cr debt and PAT margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt cost ~8.5-8.6%; PAT margin guided at ~12-13% for FY27 and ~11-13% for FY28, described as conservative and sensitive to statutory approval delays.

Capacity expansion: ~₹130 cr Anlon-site capex (~1,200 MT) targeted by Q1 FY28 but subject to statutory approvals; management flagged possible delays of one to two months changing projections.
Working capital and cash flow: receivable days of ~130-135 vs 90-day terms; management suggests a possible fundraise may be needed for the FY28 revenue ambition, which it did not confirm.

Guidance consistency: management gave differing EBITDA margin ranges (25-27%, 25-28%, 25-30%) and revenue framing; watch Q2 for reconciliation and the share-swap completion of Apiqo and Bizotic to 100% by end-Q2.

544501|2026-03.headline: Sugs Lloyd FY26 revenue rose about 70% to INR300 crore, PAT up 71% to INR28 crore, with INR825 crore unexecuted order book.
544501|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue reached INR300 crore versus INR176 crore in FY25, ahead of the INR270 crore guidance, with EBITDA up 69% and PAT up 71% to about INR28 crore. Management said margins were held broadly flat year-on-year, though Q4 margin was about 12% versus roughly 14% for the half year, which management attributed to a delayed MAHAGENCO order and related site disruption. Growth drivers were RDSS-funded transmission and distribution work and solar EPC, plus a INR640 crore (incl. 18% GST, about INR540 crore ex-GST) SCADA order from Konkan Railway. Receivables and retention balances rose, and management flagged 40% of FY26 sales coming in Q4 as a key working-capital issue.

No specific capacity or capex figures were given in the call.

Most orders carry price variation clauses covering commodity (including LME-linked copper) and statutory tax changes.

Competitors named for large SCADA projects: L&T, Voltas and other EPC players. Management said 99% of business is with government entities, and it is bidding only on centrally or multilaterally funded projects.
Geographic expansion: Odisha and Bihar were earlier core markets; now Gujarat, Maharashtra, Punjab, Chhattisgarh; international expansion planned but not immediate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 'other current assets' jump to INR42 crore, and is it retention money?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is retention money not yet due, released after the company discharges project obligations.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivables be managed, and what are the terms, working capital and margins on the large INR600 crore order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40% of sales fall in Q4, with 10% carried from prior periods. Steps include a collection task force, shifting to projects with easier payment terms, and capping retention at 10%. The large order is expected to carry no margin pressure, under RDSS payment terms.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a MAHAGENCO order delayed by a Q3 land dispute and local political interference, which raised costs; year-on-year margins described as stagnant.

544511|2026-03.headline: Karbonsteel crossed ₹300 crore revenue in FY26 with 10.86% EBITDA margin and ₹10.51 crore PAT, which management says normalises to ₹16.56 crore.
544511|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue crossed ₹300 crore, but the company missed its ₹340 crore ideal level because of Khopoli exit, labour migration after the March LPG force majeure, and a ~₹40 crore shortfall from low-value labour jobs. Reported EBITDA margin was 10.86% and PAT ₹10.51 crore, including a ₹1.65 crore NCLT bad-debt write-off, ₹2.4 crore rent for the delayed Umargam expansion and Khopoli shifting costs. segments.name: PEB
segments.commentary: Revenue contribution fell to 0%; management says it will remain a small part as the company focuses on production rather than erection.

segments.name: Railways / bullet train
segments.commentary: Bullet train work (4,500 tonnes) was largely booked in the prior year; FY26 contribution nominal. Railway product development is at a very early stage.

Labour expected to return by end-June 2026; ~₹150 crore order pipeline expected around September-October.
capex_capacity: Umargam expansion from 30,000 to 54,000 tonnes; completion revised to October (management cited 'October 2025' in places, which appears to be a transcription error given the call date of June 2026); initially targeted March.

544512|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 106.5% YoY to INR725.6 crore and FY26 PAT rose 89% to INR115.5 crore, with working capital absorbing cash.
544512|2026-03.overview: Shringar reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR725.6 crore (+106.5% YoY) with PAT of INR34 crore (+123.5%), and FY26 revenue of INR2,245.8 crore (+57.1%) and PAT of INR115.5 crore (+89%). Production capacity was raised from 2,500 kg to 4,000 kg in Q4, with FY26 utilisation at 87% on a blended 2,625 kg. The company entered bridal jewellery with Tanishq and Malabar Gold and Diamonds, and management reiterated about 30% value CAGR guidance for the next two to three years. Management acknowledged that working capital growth absorbed cash, leaving free cash flow negative, and said it expects to shift toward outright sales and organised clients within about two quarters.

Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15%; management said the increase is absorbed into domestic gold prices and has not caused distinct difficulties.
Management cited about 1 crore weddings in FY26 and weddings growing about 7-8% annually.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to notional hedging losses on MCX-hedged gold, plus about 10 exhibitions, machinery and setup costs for the new factory, and higher CSR spend.

qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 30% job work and 70% outright sales. Job work earned INR28 crore in FY26 as a labour fee. Management said converting job work to outright sales could lift revenue to INR70-80 crore on the same volume and triple profit on that volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital rise and was the cycle lengthening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outright sales require more capital, which is the trade-off for higher margin. It expects organised clients with fixed payment dates to ease cash-flow churn over time. It did not give debtor or inventory day figures.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% guidance is value growth and a minimum target. Bridal is not included in that guidance; it could push growth above 30% if bridal reaches parity with mangalsutra within three years.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to convert a significant portion of operations to outright contracts within about two quarters, which should help move cash flow from negative to positive.
