544513|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 53.8 crore; standalone revenue up 7.8% YoY to INR 42 crore, Ind AS EBITDA margin 56.3% consolidated.
544513|2026-06.overview: Standalone workspace revenue rose 7.8% YoY to INR 42 crore, with consolidated revenue at INR 53.8 crore and Ind AS consolidated EBITDA up 14.7% to INR 30.3 crore. Operational portfolio grew to 1.13 million sq ft (17,294 seats, 27 centers, 12 cities) with occupancy at 91.93%. Post-quarter, the company raised INR 100 crore of 11.75% secured NCDs (36 months) and encumbered about 19.65% of equity, with promoter holding stated at 36.81%. Management highlighted a pipeline of 2.31 million sq ft signed for future consumption, though analyst questions on Ahmedabad per-sq-ft economics, lease-inclusive leverage and Q4 margin drop were answered only partially.

segments.name: Managed workspace (standalone)
segments.commentary: INR 42 crore revenue, recurring; occupied seats 15,899 vs 12,534 YoY; occupancy 91.93% vs 88.6%. Enterprise clients ~70% of revenue vs 52% a year ago; revenue-to-rent 2.63x.

segments.name: Needle & Thread (design and build)
segments.commentary: Balance of consolidated revenue (about INR 11.8 crore implied), one-time in nature and booked on project completion/milestone under Ind AS. FY26 one-time revenue was INR 57 crore per management.

segments.name: Tier 2 cities
segments.commentary: About 80% of operational SBA in Tier 2 cities, contributing ~74% of standalone revenue in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects revenue from signed capacity to progressively show up as centers move into operation; no numerical revenue guidance given.

Ahmedabad development-management project (~8.6 lakh sq ft, Ambli Bopal Road): fit-out capex ~INR 100 crore, expected ~8,500 seats and ~INR 120 crore revenue potential once handed over; no timeline stated.
Total identified portfolio ~3.63 million sq ft across 40 centers with 52,000+ operational seats; FY27 framed as year of executing signed assets and expanding into new territories.
INR 100 crore NCD to reflect in financials from Q2 onwards; ~INR 55 crore of existing debt repaid.
Global tokenization platform being set up outside India; entity incorporation commenced, no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Operational 1.13 million sq ft; 0.19 million sq ft under fit-out; 2.31 million sq ft signed for future consumption (total identified ~3.63 million sq ft, 40 centers).

Management said ~12 lakh sq ft operational area of which ~75% is company-built, roughly 9 lakh sq ft at ~INR 1,300/sq ft, i.e., ~INR 118 crore of fit-out investment to date (excluding refurbishment and deposits on future sites).
Development-management model covers ~1.4 million sq ft across Ahmedabad and Jaipur.
New-center ramp: 75-90 days from handover to client fit-out; ~6-9 months to maturity, per management.
Management said unspent IPO proceeds are still with the company and will be deployed as properties under construction are handed over.
demand_pricing: Ahmedabad realisations management cited at INR 100-125 per sq ft per month for a full operating year; Capital One (~3.15 lakh sq ft, 95% pre-leased) became operational toward end FY26.
Analyst's implied Capital One figure of ~INR 1,044/sq ft/yr was reconciled by management to ~INR 87/sq ft/month in year one, reflecting rent-free and fit-out periods; 8-9 billable months assumed.
Enterprise/GCC demand: management said it is in talks with clients for full-spectrum GCC solutions in Bangalore and Hyderabad.
Scalex Advisory (GCC full-service JV, ~12% stake held by DevX) to focus on GIFT City; managed-office GCC leads to be redirected to DevX.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 145 crore at end FY26
vs INR 89 crore at end FY26; net debt/equity 0.4x vs 0.48x; net debt/EBITDA (IGAAP) 1.04x vs 2.10x

qa_highlights.question: Shubham Padhiyar (Chhattisgarh Investments) asked why Mumbai Central revenue fell from INR 14 crore to INR 11 crore despite Noida revenue rising, given a Noida centre closure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Noida centre closed at the very end of FY26 after litigation, and that Noida (three centres) did about INR 11.5 crore operational revenue before closure, with roughly INR 4.5 crore now lost from the closed centre. The analyst's figures were disputed (INR 9 crore vs INR 11.5-12 crore), and the reconciliation was deferred to email.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst's implied Capital One revenue of about INR 1,050 per sq ft per year (INR 2.7-3 crore a month on ~3.15 lakh sq ft) versus Ahmedabad portfolio at about INR 2,500 per sq ft per year.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Ahmedabad realisations are INR 100-125 per sq ft per month (about INR 1,200-1,500 a year), and that INR 2,500 a year is not the right figure. The INR 1,044 figure equals about INR 87 per sq ft per month in year one, reflecting rent-free and fit-out periods; management assumed 8-9 billable months. Management declined to confirm the analyst's FY26 Ahmedabad revenue of about INR 78 crore and asked for an email.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is recurring versus one-time, and how much capex has been spent on the 1.13 million sq ft portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: Of INR 53.8 crore consolidated revenue, INR 42 crore is managed office (recurring) and the balance is Needle & Thread one-time revenue. FY26 Needle & Thread one-time revenue was INR 57 crore. About 75% of the ~12 lakh sq ft is company-built, roughly 9 lakh sq ft at about INR 1,300 per sq ft, i.e. about INR 118 crore of fit-out investment, excluding refurbishment and deposits on future sites.

qa_highlights.question: Mukul Bhushan (Raru Family Office) asked to disclose lease-inclusive leverage each quarter: debt-to-equity ~2x and ROCE ~9% including about INR 226 crore of lease liability, versus the presented 0.78x and 14%.
qa_highlights.answer: Parin Shah did not confirm or refute the lease-inclusive figures. He explained the ROCE/ROE lag: 75-90 days from handover to fit-out and client onboarding, and 6-9 months to maturity. He said ROCE is 14% and ROE 7%, and that unspent IPO funds will be deployed as under-construction properties are handed over.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone EBITDA margin fall to 59.2% in Q4 from 64% a year earlier, and should the FY27 model use 60.5% or 59.2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Parin Shah attributed the Q4 drop to expenses he described as one-time in nature, and said it was not a structural margin decline. He cited standalone Ind AS margin of 66% in Q1 and peer margins of 60-65%. Consolidated margin is lower because Needle & Thread books revenue on project completion or milestone under Ind AS. No FY27 margin figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Scalex Advisory non-compete work, what is DevX's stake, and can DevX still do GCC business?
qa_highlights.answer: Umesh Uttamchandani said Scalex is a JV of DevX, Savvy (GIFT City developer) and Talati & Talati, with DevX holding about 12%. It targets full-spectrum GCC solutions, limited to GIFT City, and standalone managed-office leads are redirected to DevX. DevX continues GCC business (payroll and facility management) and is in talks for GCC solutions in Bangalore and Hyderabad.

risks_watch: Revenue reconciliation gaps: city-wise and Ahmedabad revenue figures disputed on the call and deferred to email; watch for the written responses and whether they close the gap.

Lease-inclusive leverage: the analyst's estimate of about 2x debt/equity and about 9% ROCE including about INR 226 crore of lease liabilities was not answered. Management asked for quarterly disclosure of this view to be declined; watch whether it is added.

Ramp execution: 2.31 million sq ft signed but not yet operational, with 0.19 million sq ft under fit-out. Revenue conversion timelines (75-90 days to handover-fit-out, 6-9 months to maturity) are long, and no revenue timeline for the Ahmedabad 8.6 lakh sq ft project was given.

Debt and promoter pledge: INR 100 crore 11.75% NCD over 36 months from Q2; about 19.65% of equity encumbered; promoter holding 36.81% (about 37.29% after warrant conversion) against a 19.65% covenant floor. Watch for any changes to covenants or pledge levels.

Margin trajectory: Q4 FY26 standalone margin of 59.2% vs 64% a year earlier was attributed to one-time expenses without quantification. Consolidated Ind AS margin of 56.3% is diluted by Needle & Thread's milestone-based revenue recognition.

Early-stage new ventures: tokenisation platform outside India (no timeline), AI infrastructure launchpad, and Scalex (operations only just starting, GIFT City focus). Monitor incorporation and any capital commitments.
key_quotes: So the operational number although being 1.12 million square feet, there is an additional 0.19 million square feet, which is under fit out.
It is important to note that this is not a borrowed money, there is no bank, no loan, and no repayment schedule attached to it.
Against this requirement, the current promoter shareholding is 36.81%, which is significantly above the prescribed minimum requirement.
I would appreciate if you can reach out to our email address of Investor Relations team and we would be happy to address those questions.
544513|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on portfolio growth, occupancy and the signed pipeline, but defensive and evasive when pressed on city-level revenue, Ahmedabad per-sq-ft economics, lease-inclusive leverage and the Q4 margin fall. Several specific questions were deferred to email follow-up.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone Ind AS margin 66% and consolidated Ind AS EBITDA margin 56.3% vs 47.4%, but Q4 FY26 standalone margin fell to 59.2% from 64% on unquantified one-time expenses and Needle & Thread milestone revenue dilutes consolidated margin; no FY27 margin figure given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 0.19m sq ft already under fit-out and 2.31m sq ft signed for future consumption (total identified ~3.63m sq ft, 40 centres), with 75-90 days from handover to fit-out; Ahmedabad 8.6 lakh sq ft has no timeline, so its timing stays unclear.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Occupied seats rose to 15,899 from 12,534 YoY and occupancy to 91.93% from 88.6%, with Capital One (~3.15 lakh sq ft, 95% pre-leased) ramping; enterprise share of revenue 70% vs 52%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 91.93% is above the 80% threshold, the Ahmedabad project needs ~INR 100 crore of fit-out capex, and the INR 100 crore NCD plus unspent IPO proceeds are earmarked for handovers.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical revenue guidance was given, and management declined to confirm the analyst's Ahmedabad and Capital One figures, so there is no base for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue conversion from signed space is slow (6-9 months to maturity), the Noida closure removed ~INR 4.5 crore of revenue, and city-level figures are disputed; no numerical guidance exists to cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Scalex GCC full-service JV is just starting operations (DevX ~12% stake, GIFT City focus), and the tokenisation platform and AI launchpad are at incorporation stage with no timeline.

rows.label: 2.31m sq ft signed for future consumption
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters as centres hand over
rows.why: Signed space of 2.31m sq ft against 1.13m sq ft operational means a large pipeline is still to convert, with 0.19m sq ft already under fit-out.

rows.label: Net debt down to INR 81 crore from INR 89 crore
rows.why: Net debt/EBITDA (IGAAP) fell to 1.04x from 2.10x, and gross debt is INR 135 crore after ~INR 55 crore repayment, though the INR 100 crore 11.75% NCD is added from Q2.

rows.label: Promoter pledge at 19.65% of equity against 36.81% holding
rows.why: About 19.65% of equity is encumbered, and the stated covenant floor equals that level, so any further pledge or covenant change would be a risk to watch.

tone.note: Management was confident on occupancy (91.93%), the 2.31m sq ft signed pipeline and enterprise mix, but deferred city-level revenue, Ahmedabad per-sq-ft economics, lease-inclusive leverage and the Q4 margin drop to email; analysts pressed on each of these.

544515|2026-03.headline: Urban Company Q4 FY26 NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,148 crore, with Services ex-InstaHelp adjusted EBITDA margin at 3.3% and Q4 PAT of ₹98 crore hit by InstaHelp's ₹119 crore loss.
544515|2026-03.overview: Management reported its highest-ever quarterly NTV, with Q4 NTV up 42% YoY to ₹1,148 crore and FY26 NTV up 33% to ₹4,290 crore. Core Services ex-InstaHelp grew 26% YoY to ₹808 crore with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 3.3% of NTV from 1.6% a year earlier. International (UAE and Singapore) turned profitable for FY26 at ₹6 crore, and Native narrowed its loss to ₹31 crore. InstaHelp absorbed ₹119 crore of Q4 losses, which drove reported Q4 profit to ₹98 crore; management is investing heavily in InstaHelp and held its break-even and ₹1,000 crore EBITDA targets.

financial_highlights.value: ₹131 crore (4.1% of NTV) — 3.3% of NTV for Services adjusted EBITDA as per call
financial_highlights.change: Services margin 1.6% of NTV in Q4 FY25
Entirely attributable to InstaHelp's ₹119 crore loss; ex-InstaHelp adjusted profit ₹22 crore

segments.name: Core Services (ex-InstaHelp)
segments.commentary: Q4 NTV ₹808 crore, up 26% YoY; adjusted EBITDA ₹131 crore at 4.1% of NTV (3.3% of NTV in Services overall as stated). Management said the segment was loss-making as recently as FY24.

segments.name: International (UAE + Singapore)
segments.commentary: Q4 NTV ₹211 crore (+84% YoY) despite a March UAE headwind from the Middle East conflict; FY26 NTV ₹700 crore (+75%) with FY26 EBITDA turning positive at ₹6 crore.

segments.name: Native
segments.commentary: Q4 NTV ₹89 crore (+67% YoY); FY26 NTV ₹345 crore (+122%) with loss narrowing to ₹31 crore (-8.9% of NTV) from ₹39 crore (-25.1%) in FY25.

segments.name: InstaHelp
segments.commentary: Q4 loss of ₹119 crore covering acquisition, network subsidies and onboarding; 2.7 million orders and ₹40 crore NTV in Q4, with March alone crossing 1.1 million orders. Targets EBITDA break-even by Q3 FY28.

guidance_outlook: InstaHelp EBITDA break-even target retained at Q3 FY28.
Company-level EBITDA target of ₹1,000 crore by FY31 retained.
Management will not be giving quarterly call commentary on InstaHelp dynamics; detail is in the shareholder letter.
Management expects Services adjusted EBITDA as % of NTV to keep rising, aiming for 10% over a longer horizon; progress to be judged year-on-year rather than quarter-on-quarter.
No timeline given for Native break-even; management said it is fairly confident of the trajectory.
No incremental geography planned for the foreseeable future; focus remains India, UAE, Singapore and the KSA JV.
Native targets quadrupling net revenue with water purifiers and smart electronic door locks; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: Services now covers 60-plus cities across 47 cities' hundreds of micro-markets; densification is the priority over coverage expansion.
UC Instant (30 to 60 minute service) rolled out; management says it improves partner packing efficiency and utilisation rather than reducing it.
AI used to audit 100% of proof-of-work images; 55% of partner support queries handled by AI; about 90% of code shipped with GenAI assistance.
Saudi Arabia JV showing improving margins with visibility towards profitability.
InstaHelp expansion kept calibrated; management leaning towards densifying existing micro-markets.
demand_pricing: Services NTV growth accelerated: 19% in Q2 FY26, 21% in Q3, 26% in Q4 (ex-InstaHelp).
Management said the Middle East dip was visible month-on-month but YoY growth stayed healthy and the business is nearly back to recovery.
No material disruption from the state election-related workplace displacement; handled through pre-onboarding of professionals.
Competitive intensity in InstaHelp described as irrational at times but manageable; management said it will optimise for share rather than unit-economic elegance.
AOV sensitivity described as low in Core; management said AOV can move up or down and it will be managed through tactics and strategy.
Contribution per order declined in Q4 as InstaHelp marketing and subsidies rose; management said the decline was largely due to one cost metric (cost per order).

qa_highlights.question: What is driving Services ex-InstaHelp growth to 25% in top 10 cities, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to densification flywheel effects: higher utilisation, lower travel and faster fulfilment via UC Instant, improving retention. Growth accelerated from 19% to 26% over three quarters; management wants to see more quarters before calling it a structural trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will AOV pressure and elevated competitive intensity hurt steady-state economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated its break-even and ₹1,000 crore EBITDA guardrails but declined to give a steady-state unit-economics range, citing the need to flex tactics on AOV and competition.

qa_highlights.question: What timeline and drivers exist for Native break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Native's loss narrowed to -8.9% of NTV from -14.7% earlier; management is fairly confident of break-even but gave no timeline, and said it would happen despite new product launches.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new product pipeline for Native to meet its quadrupling target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current launches are water purifiers and smart electronic door locks; no timeline set, and revenue to come from installed-base growth and retention.

qa_highlights.question: Is the InstaHelp versus core structure a concern given competitor fundraising and is there a diversification plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees a winner-take-most dynamic in trust-based services, is targeting leadership in InstaHelp, and is not worried about competitor funding; InstaHelp average rating 4.7 and retention claimed as industry-leading.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans to expand into new geographies or adjacencies?
qa_highlights.answer: No new geography planned in the foreseeable future; no experimentation in adjacencies. Focus is entirely on densifying core micro-markets.

qa_highlights.question: What was the contribution-per-order decline and cause in InstaHelp Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marketing elevated to acquire users and build the brand, including Cricket World Cup spend; all metrics improved except contribution per order, which declined largely due to one cost line.

risks_watch: InstaHelp losses (₹119 crore in Q4) and break-even target of Q3 FY28; reported profit depends on InstaHelp spend.
Competitive intensity in InstaHelp and rising AOV pressure; management declined to quantify steady-state unit economics.
Middle East conflict effects on UAE business in March and the pace of recovery.
Native break-even has no timeline; new products (water purifiers, smart locks) not yet material.
Seasonal cost spikes in Q1/Q3 marketing ahead of peak quarters, which complicates quarter-on-quarter comparisons.
Whether Services adjusted EBITDA margin can rise from 3.3% toward 10% of NTV over a multi-year horizon.
544515|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Core and International execution, and defensive on InstaHelp unit economics, where management refused to give steady-state or quarterly guidance. Management repeatedly described competitive irrationality as manageable and said it is prioritising market share over short-term margins.
key_quotes: We are investing to win, and we intend to stay in it.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Services ex-InstaHelp adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 3.3% of NTV from 1.6% a year earlier, and management expects it to keep rising toward 10% over a longer horizon, though quarterly comparisons will be noisy from Q1/Q3 marketing spikes and InstaHelp subsidies.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management is densifying existing micro-markets across 60-plus cities rather than adding coverage, and InstaHelp expansion is kept calibrated, so new capacity is hinted at only through densification, with no new plant, line or store date given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 NTV up 42% YoY to ₹1,148 crore, transacting users up 24% to 8.4 million, InstaHelp crossed 1.1 million orders in March, and Core ex-InstaHelp grew 26%, with management guiding to continued densification-led growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex plan or utilisation level (utilisation_read gives direction only, no % level) was disclosed; the asset-light model and densification-first stance point away from a discrete capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Services ex-InstaHelp NTV growth accelerated from 19% in Q2 FY26 to 21% in Q3 and 26% in Q4, but management wants more quarters before calling it structural and has held rather than raised guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: InstaHelp absorbed ₹119 crore of Q4 losses, competitive intensity is described as irrational at times, and contribution per order declined in Q4, so the InstaHelp break-even by Q3 FY28 could slip if unit economics do not improve.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Native is targeting quadrupling net revenue with water purifiers and smart electronic door locks, but no timeline was given and these products are not yet material (Native FY26 NTV ₹345 crore).

rows.label: Native loss narrowing toward break-even
rows.why: Native loss fell to -8.9% of NTV in FY26 from -25.1% in FY25 (₹31 crore vs ₹39 crore), and management is fairly confident of break-even, but gave no timeline.

rows.label: International (UAE + Singapore) and KSA JV profitability
rows.why: International FY26 NTV grew 75% to ₹700 crore with EBITDA turning positive at ₹6 crore, Q4 NTV rose 84% to ₹211 crore despite the March UAE disruption, and the KSA JV shows improving margins with visibility toward profitability.

rows.label: InstaHelp order scale-up
rows.why: InstaHelp did 2.7 million orders and ₹40 crore NTV in Q4, with March alone above 1.1 million orders, though management is not giving quarterly InstaHelp commentary.

tone.note: Management was confident on Core densification, International profitability and the 26% Services ex-InstaHelp growth, but defensive on InstaHelp unit economics, declining to give steady-state or quarterly guidance; analysts pressed on AOV pressure, competitive intensity and the Native break-even tim

544515|2026-06.headline: Urban Company Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; Services NTV grew 29% and InstaHelp loss narrowed to ₹(132) crore.
544515|2026-06.overview: Consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore and revenue rose 44% to ₹528 crore, with orders up 79% YoY to 13.2 million. Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

financial_highlights.change: +5.2 pp YoY (stated as 170 bps improvement in the margin line in the Q&A)
improved from (11.4)% a year ago (410 bps)
Loss per order ₹(346) vs ₹(447) in Q4
1.2 million new customers added in the quarter

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: NTV ₹1,056 crore, growing 29% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration (10%→19%→21%→26%→29%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 6.9% of NTV, up 5.2 pp YoY per the call; management says the 29% base was muted by unseasonal rains and monsoon in the prior year.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

segments.name: InstaHelp
segments.commentary: NTV ₹119 crore (+51% YoY), net revenue ₹95 crore (+60% YoY); adjusted EBITDA loss ₹(132) crore, or (7.3)% of NTV versus (11.4)% a year ago. Largest investment; management expects it to need 2 or more years of investment and aims for adjusted breakeven within about 18 months.

guidance_outlook: Retains guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28.
Retains guidance of ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31.
Long-term Services adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% of NTV; currently at 6.9%. Management said it is not in a rush and sees the target as achievable without trading off growth.
Management said Services will be a cash-generating business going forward and that it intends to keep it profitable; InstaHelp is expected to need 2 years or more of investment.
Management explicitly declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29% trend, saying the company does not want to set the wrong expectations.
Top-15-city TAM for InstaHelp is ₹7,000-12,000 crore NTV annually; management's base case is ₹7,000-8,000 crore and the bull case is ₹10,000-12,000 crore.
capex_capacity: InstaHelp: management said the company is investing aggressively in micro-market density, with the investment level still under evaluation.
Core Services trainer and infrastructure capacity is being scaled up with AI support; management says the company is 'all hands on deck' as supply grows.
Beauty segment: partners are being retrained and retooled, and the company moved to a majority of professionals having access to two-wheelers, with the target of approaching 100%.

Services is expected to consume less capital as InstaHelp is scaled; management said capital allocation will be reviewed once InstaHelp approaches adjusted breakeven (hopefully within about 18 months).
demand_pricing: Management said Q1 was among the best quarters in the company's history, with growth broad-based.

InstaHelp pricing: sustainable professional payout is about ₹130-160 per hour, with ₹150 as the rule of thumb. Management said an AOV of about ₹300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even, with ₹200 per hour required to clear gross breakeven.

Management said competitors in the InstaHelp category have pricing of ₹80-120 per hour for full-month subscriptions and that competitive intensity is high; it said the company has no reason to comment on rival strategies.
Management said the 3 major players have limited their household coverage to about 3.5-4 million households; the company believes most spending goes to subsidised repeat orders.
Management said the company has 'underestimated' the Tier 2 opportunity, with Tier 2 cities performing as well as Tier 1.

Management said it is seeing acceleration in MAUs, DAUs and MTUs, with conversion rates improving; the marketing spend in Services was about ₹25 crore in the quarter versus ₹24 crore a year ago (flat).

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: is the Cheaper, Faster, Better flywheel now visible enough to call a bold trajectory shift in Services NTV growth, and can growth be guided higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flywheel comes from densifying many micro-markets, which improves partner utilisation, lowers churn and supports trust. It cited UC Instant (30-60 minute service) as a new driver. It declined to give growth guidance, said the 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base from unseasonal rains and monsoon, and said the margin of 6.9% is in line with the 9-10% long-term target, which is not a trade-off against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: why should InstaHelp get capital and attention, and how will capital be allocated over two years between Services, new segments and international?
qa_highlights.answer: InstaHelp is strategically relevant because its high frequency keeps users on the app weekly. Services is to be profitable and cash generating; UAE and Singapore are profitable wholly owned subsidiaries; the Saudi JV is nearing profitability. InstaHelp needs two years or more of investment, with capital allocation revisited at adjusted breakeven, hopefully within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: why not export the UAE and Saudi model to new international markets, given Core Services is generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited bandwidth as the main constraint. It said playbooks need local customisation plus some luck, and that earlier Australia and US launches did not succeed. It will stay focused on UAE, Saudi Arabia and India, with no plans for new international markets for now.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: where does Services margin go from 6.9% of NTV versus the 9-10% target, and would the company cap margin around 10% or reinvest?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is to reach the 9-10% range without rushing and without trading growth for margin. Priority one is growing fast, priority two is margin expansion. Once it reaches about 10%, it will decide whether to lift margins further or reinvest for faster growth.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: is the InstaHelp TAM structurally lower, and would the company operate at a narrow loss if competition leaves room for only two players?
qa_highlights.answer: The base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore NTV and the bull case is INR 10,000-12,000 crore, with 3 orders per user per month. Management said the 3 major players have limited coverage to about 3.5-4 million households and that subsidised repeat orders dominate spend. It expects a low single-digit market share outcome and says it will not spend heavily on the category to drive share, while being opinionated about winning micro-markets.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: what AOV is needed for InstaHelp to break even, and is there scope for growth above 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable professional payout is INR 130-160 per hour, with INR 150 as the rule of thumb. Gross breakeven needs about INR 200 per hour, and an AOV of about INR 300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even. Management said breakeven could take a couple of years or up to 5 years, and it declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29%.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: how is AI being used and how much margin benefit is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 90-95% of the code is now written by AI, and that support, supply-side onboarding, quality audits and fraud detection are increasingly AI-led. Marketing and Finance/HR run AI end-to-end. It said the margin benefit has started to show but there is a long way to go.

qa_highlights.question: Kotak: is Beauty acceleration sustainable, and are the 30-40 annual transactions per user assumption and consolidation prospects realistic?

544525|2026-03.headline: GK Energy FY26 standalone revenue rose 40% to INR 1,532.54 crore, with EBITDA margin at 20.44% and PAT at INR 201 crore.

Installations of 61,000+ systems in FY26 (up 34%) fell short of the 70,000-75,000 guidance, which management attributed to rainfall in Maharashtra and raw material delays in late March. 544525|2026-06.headline: GK Energy Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 71.1% YoY to INR 505 crore, with PAT up 61.6% to INR 59.7 crore.
544525|2026-06.overview: GK Energy reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue, with standalone revenue of INR 505 crore (up 71.1% YoY), EBITDA of INR 86.1 crore (margin 17.05%, up 47.7%) and PAT of INR 59.7 crore (up 61.6%). Order book stood at INR 541 crore as of June/early August 2026, including orders received after June. Installations more than doubled to 24,118 systems, and 109 MW of renewable capacity was commissioned, taking the cumulative base to over 164,500 systems and 726 MW. Management reiterated FY27 revenue doubling and PAT in double digits, with the PM-KUSUM 2.0 tender expected in Q3 as the key dependency.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reach about INR 3,000 crore revenue in the remaining three quarters?

qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed lower realisation per pump but higher total volume. It expects realisation to stay flat unless PM-KUSUM 2.0 specifications change.

qa_highlights.answer: Management is not clear on backward integration, since manufacturing capacity already exists in the market. It said further product additions are under consideration and PM-KUSUM is one of several drivers.

544526|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 111% to INR 45,484 million, but Q4 EBITDA margin compressed sharply on input-cost inflation and rupee depreciation.
544526|2026-03.overview: Saatvik reported record FY26 revenue of INR 45,484 million (up about 111% YoY), EBITDA of INR 5,811 million (12.78% margin) and PAT of INR 3,571 million (7.85% margin). Q4 revenue hit a record INR 16,077 million, but EBITDA fell to INR 1,166 million and PAT to INR 604 million, as silver, aluminium, copper and oil-linked input costs rose and the rupee weakened after the war that began 20 February 2026. Management said fixed-price contracts could not pass on these increases immediately. Cell capacity expansion is the main near-term story: 2.4 GW cell line is targeted to start production in H2 FY27, and the cell plan is now 6 GW.

544526|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn (from INR 9,157 mn YoY) on 334 MW sales; EBITDA margin rose to 8.33% while confirmed order book stands at ~6.35 GW.
544526|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a weak quarter: sales of 334 MW were down from 579 MW a year earlier and 1,050 MW in Q4 FY26, as customers deferred procurement and management chose to execute only margin-accretive orders. Revenue fell to INR 5,110 mn and PAT to INR 54 mn. Management said the EBITDA margin of 8.33% was better than the 7.25% in Q4 FY26. The Odisha cell line (2.4 GW) is near ramp-up with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026, and management is pinning margin recovery on cell volumes in H2 FY27. Management kept FY27 guidance unchanged, but the call contained no numbers for Q2.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational module capacity is 4.8 GW. Q1 sales were 334 MW against production of 408 MW. Management said the module market has become crowded.

segments.name: Non-module business (EPC, IPP, storage, B2C, transformers)
segments.commentary: Non-module revenue was 4-5% of total, with a target of 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1 and the transformer market is about INR 30,000 crore, targeted at INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 3.5-4 GW sales, revenue of about INR 6,000 crore, EBITDA margin of about 12%, PAT margin of 6-7%.
Management expects cell-led margin expansion in H2 FY27 and said cell EBITDA impact would be in the 'high double digits' (number not quantified).
ALMM-2 implementation was postponed from 1 July 2026 to 1 January 2027 because of domestic cell shortages.
FY28 guidance to be discussed in Q3 FY27. Management called FY28 a 'milestone year' as utility DCR demand starts from April 2027.

capex_capacity: Odisha Phase 1 (57 acres): 2.4 GW cell and 4 GW module. About INR 1,000 crore of capex incurred so far; Phase 1 total is about INR 1,850 crore.
Phase 2 (27 acres): 3.6 GW cell, taking total cell capacity to 6 GW. Site work to start by end-Q2 FY27, completion by end-FY28, capex about INR 1,600-1,700 crore.
Phase 3: 6 GW ingot and wafer, targeted for FY29 and aligned with ALMM-3. Planning has started.
Total capex across the programme is roughly INR 3,500 crore. Peak net debt is expected at INR 2,200-2,400 crore.
Cell line ramp-up expected by end-August or early September 2026, with ALMM-2 inspection planned for September 2026.
demand_pricing: Confirmed order book of about 6.35 GW (about 132% of 4.8 GW module capacity), valued at about INR 8,200 crore per management, with execution over 12-18 months.
Mix: about 70% utility and 30% C&I/open access. About 30% of orders are DCR. Retail is excluded from the book and runs at about 20% of monthly sales.
Pricing: about 30% of C&I orders are fixed-price. In utility, about 30-40% are variable-price (cost pass-through) and the rest fixed-price.
New orders: INR 138 crore module order in July 2026 (execution by December 2026) and about INR 400 crore accepted by a subsidiary on 11 August 2026 (execution by March 2027).
DCR cell margins are quoted at 18-20%. Management said spot cell-purchase orders are not in the order book.
Customers deferred purchases amid the Iran war, cost volatility and ALMM-1 vs ALMM-2 uncertainty. Management said demand was weak in May-June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp YoY EBITDA margin compression despite a strong order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a crowded module market, higher commodity, freight and forex costs from the geopolitical situation, and weak customer demand. It also said it declined to execute orders where input costs could not be passed on. Q1 margin of 8.33% was better than Q4 FY26's 7.25%.

qa_highlights.question: When does cell manufacturing start and what utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramp-up is expected by end-August or early September 2026, with 200 MW per month from the 2.4 GW line. Management expects about 80% utilisation by Q4 FY27. Full ramp-up is expected in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Debt peak and capex needs for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is about INR 1,250 crore. Capex incurred is about INR 1,000 crore out of a roughly INR 3,500 crore programme. Net debt is expected to peak at INR 2,200-2,400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did demand slow in Q1 when the ALMM transition was expected to pull volumes forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said developers waited because input costs rose after the Iran war began on 20 February, and force majeure notices and expected DCR extensions pushed projects out. Two tariff regimes (before and after 30 June) also encouraged waiting, which left demand subdued in May and June.

qa_highlights.question: Could you give the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give FY28 numbers until Q3 FY27. It said large utility projects tendered from December 2025 (18-24 month cycles) will drive DCR demand from April 2027, making FY28 a milestone year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the non-module business plan and transformer opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-module business is 4-5% of revenue, targeted at 7-8% in FY27 and 15% next year. Melcon was acquired mid-Q1. Management targets 8-10% of a transformer market of about INR 30,000 crore (INR 55,000 crore by 2031) and INR 1,000-1,500 crore revenue in 3-4 years.

risks_watch: Cell line ramp-up timing: management guided to ramp-up by end-August or early September 2026 and ALMM-2 inspection in September 2026, with cell volumes expected to drive H2 FY27 margins; any slip would push back the margin recovery case.

Margin pressure: Q1 EBITDA margin of 8.33% was attributed to a crowded module market and geopolitical commodity, freight and forex costs; management said Q2 margins would stay under the same pressure even with higher volumes.

Demand timing: Q1 sales of 334 MW were weak; management tied recovery to utility DCR demand from April 2027 and a 6.35 GW order book executed over 12-18 months, so FY28 visibility depends on that timing.
Balance sheet: debt about INR 1,250 crore, capex incurred about INR 1,000 crore of roughly INR 3,500 crore, and net debt expected to peak at INR 2,200-2,400 crore; debt-to-equity 0.99x.

ALMM-2 postponed from 1 July 2026 to 1 January 2027; further policy changes or delays would affect the cell-led margin thesis. Also monitor the Q2 FY27 numbers, which management did not quantify, and the encapsulant and equipment announcement expected next quarter.
key_quotes: We believe this is the right approach for the business. Our objective is not to pursue volumes at any cost, but to build a sustainable business with healthy economics and long-term value creation.
So this will immediately give a higher EBITDA in our second half of the year.
Difficult to give a number, but it's going to be in the high-double digits that is what we can say right now.
So maybe we can talk about FY28 in the third quarter.
So we feel that FY28 will be a milestone year for us and for the industry.

544527|2026-03.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q4 FY26 revenue rose 81.7% YoY to INR747.6 crore with EBITDA margin near 20%; FY26 term debt fully repaid.
544527|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR747.6 crore (+81.7% YoY, +58.5% QoQ), with EBITDA of INR149.6 crore (19.99% margin vs 16.7% a year earlier) and PAT of INR102.2 crore (+128.9% YoY). Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR1,851.5 crore (+48.8%), EBITDA INR344.4 crore (18.6% margin, +300 bps) and PAT INR201.8 crore (+70.1%). All term loans were repaid by 31 March 2026, and the Vadod unit 4 received PGCIL approval for up to 400 kV on 2 April 2026. Management flagged a planned inventory drawdown ahead of April maintenance shutdowns and a mineral oil shortage in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict.

Three new demand verticals cited: BESS, data centres and renewables. No data centre order in the book yet; BESS orders are in the order book. HVDC not targeted for now.
Competitive landscape: management argues demand will exceed supply for at least five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement sustainable given the EHV mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins on 220 kV and below are stable; the gain came from 220 kV scale-up. Margins expected to stay stable going forward.

qa_highlights.question: How is realisation rising from INR7 to INR8 lakh per MVA if EHV will reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-MVA pricing is linked to commodity prices (steel, copper, oil) via customer contracts, so it rises with commodities; it will fall as 500 MVA class 400/765 kV units come in.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for 765 kV and tank/radiator capex and debt drawdown?
qa_highlights.answer: 765 kV is at marketing stage with prototyping this year; orders won this year would be invoiced next year. Tank and radiator facility starts this FY with benefits next year; term loan may be drawn if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Vadod utilisation trajectory and revenue from higher kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation 39% in FY26, 65% in FY27, 100% in FY28; most FY27 output still 220 kV with some 400 kV.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin gap between 400 kV and 220 kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 400/765 kV margins about 200 bps higher; no 400 kV revenue yet.

qa_highlights.question: Data centre order share and HVDC plans?
qa_highlights.answer: No data centre order in the book; management is in talks with customers. HVDC not targeted until 400/765 kV prototypes are validated.

qa_highlights.question: Share of order book on price variation and any Q4 commodity hit?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of the INR2,493 crore order book has price variation; no commodity hit in Q4, and no hit is expected in Q1 as far as management can see.

qa_highlights.question: Margin accretion from backward integration and higher kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Backward integration is for supply chain control and quality, not margin; margins expected to remain fairly stable after 400/765 kV development costs.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timelines of the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: 220 kV and below takes 12-18 months; 80-85% of the current order book executes in FY27. Small 400 kV portion delivers from December to March.

qa_highlights.question: Transformer demand thumb rule per GW and BESS opportunity size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites 8-11x transformer capacity per GW generation, expected to tilt higher with BESS; BESS sizing not quantified for Atlanta.

544527|2026-06.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore; record order inflow of INR972.42 crore lifted order book to INR3,116.63 crore.
544527|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore, driven mainly by volume from newly commissioned plants, with management saying pricing and product mix were broadly unchanged. Gross margin rose 130 bps to 27.3% and EBITDA margin expanded to 16.5% from 15.5% a year ago, though both moderated from Q4 FY26 seasonally. Order inflow was a record INR972.42 crore, taking the unexecuted order book to about INR3,117 crore, of which about INR2,400 crore is expected to execute in FY27. Management reiterated a 40% revenue CAGR target and a 17-18% margin range, while 400 kV and 765 kV product timelines were pushed out and largely remain conditional.

segments.commentary: 220 kV class was 56% of Q1 revenue, 66 kV class 25%, and 132 kV class about 5.5%. Power transformers were about 79% of revenue, with auto, inverter duty and other products making up the balance.

segments.name: End market
segments.commentary: Transmission and distribution contributed about 66% of revenue and renewable energy about 19%, with thermal power and other industrial making up the rest.

segments.name: Order book by voltage
segments.commentary: 220 kV and above transformers are over 55% of the order book; 400 kV transformers and reactors account for nearly INR275 crore. Management said the entire record Q1 inflow is 220 kV and below.

EBITDA margin expected around 17-18% for the year, with raw material inflation expected to persist but margins sustainable at the Q1 level.
About INR2,400 crore of the ~INR3,100 crore unexecuted order book is due for execution in FY27.
Inverter duty transformer facility (~5,000 MVA) targeted for commissioning by end-December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new 400 kV capacity pressure incremental margins or order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Niral Patel said Q1 was the highest order inflow in at least 2-2.5 years, with no visible pricing correction in the market.

544530|2026-09.headline: Anand Rathi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR2,732 million and PAT rose 50% to INR419 million, a record quarter per management.
544530|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR2,732 million, with PAT up 50% YoY to INR419 million at a 15% margin. H1 revenue rose 21% to INR5,193 million; H1 PAT after exceptional items was INR653 million (up 29%), and PAT before exceptional items was INR810 million (up 60%). Broking and related services grew 34% YoY to INR1,551 million, while the MTF book reached INR14,993 million at 30 September, already about 57% of the year-end guidance. Management said market volumes were weak in derivatives but cash volumes were improving, and it discussed the drop in net cash, which it attributed to clients moving margins from FDs into G-Secs.

financial_highlights.metric: Broking and related services revenue (Q2 FY27)
Broking and related services revenue (H1 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: Q2 distribution income up about 4% YoY per analyst question; not confirmed by management

segments.name: Broking and related services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR1,551 million (+34% YoY); H1 INR2,831 million (+25% YoY). Equity cash is 52% of broking revenue. Digital platform contributed 36% of brokerage income in H1.

segments.name: Margin trading facility (MTF)
segments.commentary: Book INR14,993 million at 30 Sep 2026 against year-end guidance of INR17,500-18,000 million. Q2 MTF book grew 38% YoY to INR1,499 crore; MTF interest income INR496 million in Q2 (+36%) and INR924 million in H1 (+43%). Borrowing cost about 9.5%, NIM about 4.5%, zero NPAs, average book per client below INR17 lakh.

segments.name: Distribution and non-broking
segments.commentary: Distribution AUM INR99,990 million, up 29% YoY. Distribution income INR327 million in Q2 and INR603 million in H1. Trail income now covers about 75% of salary costs, per management.

segments.commentary: Asset management grew 29% YoY to INR99,990 million. Under custody grew about 13% YoY to about INR1.15 trillion.

Distribution AUM to grow about 40% by end of FY27; management said it had already reached 29% growth by September.
Broking revenue targeted to grow 15-20% and non-broking 30-35% (up to 40% in some cases).
Long-term target: top line growth of about 15-20% and bottom line growth of about 20-25% to 30%.

Client base about 10.5 lakh, of which 55% have been with the firm for more than 3 years and 71% of active clients are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

New products: insurance is being stabilised, AIF is being added to distribution, and an NRI business is being built.
demand_pricing: Nifty 50 fell 5.22% in the quarter and 1.3% in H1, including a 6% fall in September. IPO activity was strong: 108 IPOs raised about INR90,000 crore in Q2, and H1 raised INR96,585 crore across 154 mainboard IPOs.
Industry MTF book was INR156,261 crore as of 12 Oct 2026, up about 41% YoY. Demat accounts were about 24 crore, with 31.1 lakh added in September.

Management said cash-market volumes were improving while F&O and capital-market volumes were flat to lower. It said Anand Rathi's broking growth outperformed the industry because it has no proprietary trading volumes.
Distribution income growth lagged AUM growth because of upfront commissions in the prior year and the RBI/AMFI ARN transfer cooling period, which was extended from 6 to 12 months.
Around INR300 crore of MTF-related impact from an RBI circular was absorbed, and borrowing costs were held at around 9.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did distribution income grow only 4% when distribution AUM grew 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed upfront commissions earned in the prior year that did not repeat, plus a longer 12-month ARN transfer cooling period. It said trail income is rising and now covers about 75% of salaries.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise about 31% in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outsourced staff were moved onto the payroll, which it called largely one-time. It also said it keeps adding RMs and product staff, about 150 employees on an ongoing basis.

qa_highlights.question: Have trading volumes recovered since Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash-market volumes were growing consistently while derivatives and capital-market volumes were static or lower. Broking revenue is tracking cash volumes.

qa_highlights.question: How is MTF spread and risk managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing cost is about 9.5% and NIM about 4.5%. Average book per client is below INR17 lakh, and the company says its MTF NPA has been zero for 8 years. Policy has not changed; the stock list is about 1,000 approved stocks out of about 2,000 permitted.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net cash fall from about INR2,700 crore to about INR900 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HNI clients moved margin cash from FDs into G-Secs following an RBI circular. Business is intact, and the decline reflects a change in the form of client margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt-market strategy with yields above 7.40%?

rows.why: Net cash fell from about INR2,700 crore to about INR900 crore as HNI clients moved margin cash from FDs into G-Secs, a change management called format-only, though it could still affect interest income.

rows.why: Trail income now covers about 75% of salary costs, and the ARN cooling period went from 6 to 12 months, so distribution income should catch up only if trail income compounds on AUM up 29%.

544531|2026-03.headline: True Colors FY26 revenue rose 29.22% to INR 301.55 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.58% and PAT at INR 31.16 crore, but operating cash flow was negative.

544532|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 235% YoY to INR591 crore, but EBITDA margin was 12.1% and FY26 PAT margin 8.5%, below the 11% promised earlier.
544532|2026-03.overview: Solarworld reported Q4 FY26 revenue from operations of INR591 crore (up 235% YoY), EBITDA of INR73 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT of INR49 crore (8.1% net margin). For FY26, total income was INR1,416 crore (up 1.57% YoY), EBITDA INR187.9 crore (13.3%) and PAT INR120.4 crore (8.5%). Management blamed a loss-making initial module ramp after ALMM approval in December 2025 and sharp raw material cost increases in Q4 linked to the West Asia conflict. The company is pivoting toward BESS, with a 582 MWac / 1.2 GWh DC BESS project pipeline and a 3.4 GW BESS line in trials.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 EPC revenue about INR1,250 crore; management cites EPC PAT margin close to 10.5%. EPC margin guided at 9-11% through the cycle and 8-11% overall for FY27. Solar EPC order book about INR1,674 crore.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: FY26 BESS revenue was nil; management guides INR800-1,000 crore in FY27. BESS order book about INR1,136 crore. Q4 orders from NTPC at Solapur and Unchahar aggregate about 514 MWh, order value about INR5 billion incl. O&M. BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT.

segments.name: Solar module manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.5 GW Roorkee module line began operations after ALMM approval in December 2025; about two to two-and-a-half months of run-time in FY26 produced a slight loss. Breakeven at about 30-35% utilisation; FY26-27 utilisation expected at 40-45% on about 600 MW captive NTPC REL orders, rising to 60-65% with more orders. Line capex about INR146 crore.

Management expects 40-45% revenue growth in FY27 and says it will not sustain FY26's 200-250% growth.

BESS margin guided at 14-15% PBT; 3.4 GW BESS line capex about INR55-60 crore, potential revenue about INR3,000 crore at full capacity (740 containers at INR4.5 crore each).
Q1 and Q2 seasonally weak; Q3 and Q4 strong. Management declined to give a half-yearly split.
1.2 GW solar cell line at Pandhurna targeted for commercial operation by June 2027; cell-line funds to be deployed from Q3 FY27.
No near-term plans to add module or cell capacity until about 75-80% captive utilisation is visible.

Raw material costs up sharply since Oct 2025: copper about +40%, aluminium about +50%, steel higher; INR depreciated from about 85-86 to about 96 per USD, affecting BESS imported inputs.
ALMM List-II (cells) applies from June 2026; management expects 90-95% of projects to shift to DCR cells, with a possible 6-12 month cell shortage.
Current order book has no ALMM-2 cell requirement, giving a headway of about a year. Lithium cells for BESS are sourced from China as no Indian supplier exists.
PPA signing delays after L1 bids and grid connectivity constraints are slowing the solar tender market; management expects connectivity to take 10-12 more months to resolve.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said EPC PAT margin is about 10.5%, with the module loss from a short ramp and Q4 raw material headwinds dragging the total. Guidance is INR1,900-2,000 crore revenue and 8-11% overall margins.

qa_highlights.question: Battery cell unit timeline, and when will it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1.2 GW cell line at Pandhurna is now targeted for commercial start by June 2027, with construction starting around June 2026.

qa_highlights.answer: Other expense rose to INR83 million from INR74 million; last year's base included a INR140 million write-off that was recovered this year. The 3.4 GW BESS line capex is INR55-60 crore; margin 14-15% PBT.

qa_highlights.question: How will the module line utilisation ramp, and what is breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven is around 30-35% utilisation. Utilisation should reach 40-45% on existing NTPC REL orders (about 600 MW), rising to 60-65% with new orders. All existing EPC orders can be serviced in-house.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company expand module or cell capacity, and why are PPAs being rescinded?
qa_highlights.answer: No expansion planned until 75-80% captive use is visible. PPA delays stem from DISCOM absorption and transmission constraints; management expects resolution by around end-FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: ROW compensation is moving to market rates, which helps, but management does not see it as the biggest hurdle; no major labour issues. Tender activity is slower, but the company's order book is full.

544540|2026-06.headline: EPACK Prefab Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~25% to INR366 crore, with EBITDA margin down ~100 bps to 9.4% on steel costs and order book at INR1,380 crore.
544540|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew about 25% YoY to INR366 crore from INR295 crore, and EBITDA rose to nearly INR35 crore from INR30.9 crore. EBITDA margin fell to 9.4% from 10.5%, which management attributed to steel price increases linked to the Middle East conflict, partly offset by fixed-price contract repricing and purchasing policy. Order inflow was INR580 crore versus INR240 crore a year earlier, and the order book stood at about INR1,376-1,380 crore as of 30 June 2026. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-1,950 crore (about 30% growth) and a 10.5-11.5% EBITDA margin from Q2 onwards, and announced a data center subsidiary with INR75 crore planned equity.

segments.commentary: Order book for sandwich panels is about 3.2 lakh sq m on the Mambattu continuous line, or about 4.7 lakh sq m including Greater Noida and Mambattu, per the Q&A. Utilisation was 44% in Q1, and management expects 70-75%+ for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Share of fixed-price vs pass-through orders in the current book?
qa_highlights.answer: Most orders are fixed-price; management manages risk by booking orders weekly at current prices. Steel rose 12-15% but the balance-sheet impact was about 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 10-11% and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects improvement from Q2 and full-year EBITDA margin of ~10.5%. Q1 dip was ~100 bps against an earlier estimate of ~200 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Data center revenue potential, working capital, and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify until end-Q1 numbers are available and said the funding plan is undecided, with any debt expected to be modest.

qa_highlights.question: Sandwich panel order book fell from 4 lakh to 3.2 lakh sq m QoQ; is utilisation still rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Correction: 4 lakh sq m covered Greater Noida and Mambattu. Mambattu continuous line alone has 3.2 lakh sq m, and total including Greater Noida is about 4.7 lakh sq m. Even without new orders, the line would reach 70%+ annualised utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Win rate of ~20%: what drives the rate and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it bids on 30-40% of quotes and selects projects, and losses come partly from capacity constraints by region. A 20% win rate is said to be strong against 10-12% peers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company sustain 30% growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited India fabrication demand of 12-19% of steel output, ~36 million tonnes by 2030 in the pessimistic case, and suggested EPACK's 0.3-0.35 million tonnes is a small share.

risks_watch: Margin recovery to 10.5-11.5% from Q2 depends on repricing and new orders at post-war steel prices; Q1 margin was 9.4% and management said the impact was about 100 bps versus an earlier estimate of about 200 bps.
Most orders are fixed-price with no pass-through; steel rose 12-15% since the war began. Booking weekly at current prices is the main protection, so a further steel spike could hit margins again.

Capacity ramp-up timing: Ghiloth sandwich panel line due end-Q1 with production from Q2, Mambattu second AP line from Q2, Gujarat (~50,000 tpa) in Q4 FY27 with production from April 2027. Monsoon-related civil works delays were flagged as a Q2 execution risk.

Order book coverage: opening book INR1,110 crore on 1 April 2026 and order book INR1,376-1,380 crore at 30 June 2026 against FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,900-1,950 crore; FY27 order inflow target of INR2,000 crore, with INR580 crore booked in Q1 and management expecting more than 50% in H1. Win rate of about 20% and the sandwich panel order book (3.2 lakh sq m Mambattu line) need to be tracked.
